issue.title: off-clock link chips 200-link Live Preview 35 ms wall-clock assertion flakes under full npm test load
issue.description:
Proposed by bob-cli-js.4 note #1 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP) and observed earlier by bob-cli-js.1 (note #2), triaged by the bob-cli-js land agent.

- bob-cli-js.4--3: the full bob-plugins `npm test` run (5,933 tests) failed this assertion twice, at 50.6 ms and 36.3 ms against the 35 ms threshold. Running the test file alone passed at 9.4 ms.
- bob-cli-js.1--1: a full `npm test` run (5,923 tests) failed the same 200-link timing assertion, which then passed in isolation.
- Land agent on bob-plugins 0fd19de: `node --test scripts/test-ledger-tools-off-clock-link-chips.cjs` passed 56/56 three times in a row.

Fail rate: 2 of 2 reported full-suite runs (parallel `node --test` over ~300 files) versus 0 of 4+ isolated serial runs. Neither epic phase touched off-clock chip code.

Cause, from the source (scripts/test-ledger-tools-off-clock-link-chips.cjs, test added in 23d401b): the test times one warm build with `performance.now()` around the work and asserts `elapsed < 35`, so scheduler delay under suite load counts as algorithm time. This is the same measurement pattern as bob-cli-io (frees-marks, 25 ms), but on a different test node. Keep the deterministic memoization assertions and keep a meaningful regression gate, for example the minimum of several samples or a counted-work assertion, without blindly raising the threshold.
